1
Before You Start

To create your import files, you need:

2
Download Reports from Sports Affinity

You need two reports from the Sports Affinity Association site. Both come from the same page — you just select a different report from the dropdown.

Navigate to Sports Affinity

  1. Go to ayso.sportsaffinity.com and log in with your Sports Connect credentials. (Or from Sports Connect, click your profile in the upper right corner and select "Go to AYSO.")
  2. Navigate to Players / Admins → Player Lookup

Set Your Filters

  1. Season: Select the current membership year from the dropdown to the left of "PLAYER LOOKUP" (e.g., "2025-2026 MY2025")
  2. Select Region: Choose your region
  3. Select Age Group: Set to "Multiple" and select all age groups
  4. Leave other filters at defaults (All Play Types, All Genders, All for Accepted)

Download Report 1: "Player Detail | upload format"

This is your primary data source — player names, DOB, gender, parent contacts, addresses, and team assignments.

  1. Click the Report dropdown (top right of the player list)
  2. Select "Player Detail | upload format" from the dropdown menu
Select "Player Detail | upload format" from the Report dropdown
  1. Click Print — a new window opens with the report in a table format
  2. In the report window, select "Excel" from the format dropdown (top left of the report)
  3. Click Export

Select "Excel" from the format dropdown

Click Export to download the file

The file downloads as playerUpload.xlsx

  1. Save the file to the same folder as the import tool

Download Report 2: "Player Photo BC Info"

This report shows actual birth certificate upload and verification dates per player — the definitive source for who has a BC on file.

This report is accessed from a different location than Report 1:

  1. In Sports Affinity, click Reports in the top menu bar — a dropdown of report categories appears
Click "Reports" in the top navigation — the report categories dropdown appears
  1. Click "Player Reports" to expand the player report options
Select "Player Reports" from the dropdown categories
  1. From the report list, select "Player Photo BC Info"
Select "Player Photo BC Info" from the Reports dropdown — note this is under Reports, not Players/Admins
  1. Set Area and Region filters to your region
  2. Leave Date Range blank (to get all players)
  3. Click "Generate Report"
  4. In the report viewer, select "Excel" from the format dropdown
  5. Click Export
Select Excel format and click Export (player data blurred for privacy)
  1. Save the file — it typically downloads as Player_Photo_BC_Info.xlsx or Player Photo BC Info.xlsx (the tool handles both naming conventions)
💡 What This Report Shows Each player row includes: Birth Certificate Uploaded (date the file was uploaded) and Birth Certificate Verified (date someone reviewed it). If either date is present, the player has a BC on file. The import tool uses these dates — not the unreliable "Media" column from the Applications report.
💡 Where Do These Reports Come From? Both reports are generated from the Sports Affinity (Association) site at ayso.sportsaffinity.com, NOT the Sports Connect Registration site. Report 1 is under Players/Admins → Player Lookup → Report dropdown. Report 2 is under Reports → Player Reports.
3
Download Prior Years (Optional — Recommended)

To capture returning players who may have sat out a season, you can include prior years' data. The import tool will merge them, deduplicate by player name + DOB, and keep the most recent contact information.

Why bother? A player who played in 2024 but skipped 2025 still has a valid birth certificate on file. If they come back for 2026, importing them means they won't have to re-upload their BC.

How to Download Prior Years

  1. Go back to the Player Lookup page on Sports Affinity
  2. Change the Season dropdown to the prior year (e.g., "2024-2025 MY2024")
  3. Keep all other filters the same
  4. Download both reports again (Player Detail | upload format + All Player Applications Detail)
  5. Save them with distinguishable names (e.g., playerUpload_2024.xlsx, Player_Photo_BC_Info_2024.xlsx)
  6. Repeat for additional years if desired (2023-2024 MY2023, etc.)
⚠️ Diminishing Returns After 3 Years Players from 3+ years ago are less likely to return, and their contact info is more likely outdated. Two years of history (current + prior year) is a good balance. Three years is the practical maximum.
4
Run the PlayMetrics Import Tool

The tool handles all data transformation automatically — phone formatting, ZIP code truncation, gender mapping, BC status determination, age filtering, and the file split.

Open a Terminal

You need a command prompt to run the tool. Here's how to open one:

PlatformHow to Open
Windows 10/11Open File Explorer, navigate to the folder with your files. Click the address bar, type cmd, and press Enter. A command prompt opens in that folder.
MacOpen Terminal (search "Terminal" in Spotlight with ⌘+Space). Type cd (with a space), then drag the folder from Finder into the Terminal window — it fills in the path. Press Enter.

Option A: Batch Mode (Recommended)

Point to a folder containing all your SA report files — no prompts, auto-detects everything:

Windows: PlayMetricsImport.exe --dir C:\path\to\your\reports
Mac / Linux: python3 playmetrics_import.py --dir /path/to/your/reports

Option B: Interactive Mode

Run without arguments and the tool will prompt you for each file:

Windows: PlayMetricsImport.exe
Mac / Linux: python3 playmetrics_import.py
💡 Windows SmartScreen Warning The first time you run the .exe, Windows may show "Windows protected your PC." This is normal for unsigned applications. Click "More info" → "Run anyway" to proceed. This only happens once.

With --dir, the tool scans the folder for all playerUpload*.xlsx and Player*Photo*BC*.xlsx files, loads them all, and merges multiple seasons automatically — no prompts. Without it, the tool walks you through file selection step by step.

What the Tool Does

  1. Auto-detects playerUpload*.xlsx and Player Photo BC*.xlsx files (handles underscores, spaces, and year suffixes like _2025)
  2. Prompts you to add additional seasons' files (if you downloaded prior years)
  3. Merges multi-season data, deduplicating by player name + DOB
  4. Filters out aged-out players (born before Aug 1, 2007 for Fall 2026)
  5. Blanks team column — prior season teams don't exist in PM; teams built fresh after draft
  6. Determines BC status from the Applications report Media column (B = BC on file)
  7. Formats phones (XXX-XXX-XXXX), ZIPs (5 digits), DOBs (MM/DD/YYYY)
  8. Splits output into BC-verified and non-verified CSV files

What the Tool Produces

Three files in a playmetrics_output/ folder:

FileWhat It IsWhat To Do With It
playmetrics_bc_verified_YYYYMMDD.csvPlayers with BC on fileSend to PlayMetrics (success@playmetrics.com). They import and flag as verified.
playmetrics_non_verified_YYYYMMDD.csvPlayers without BCImport yourself in PM admin. These players will be prompted to upload during registration.
playmetrics_all_players_YYYYMMDD.csvCombined reference copyDo not import. For your records only.

Field Mapping (SA → PlayMetrics)

PlayMetrics ColumnSource (SA playerUpload)Transformation
player_first_namePlayerFirstNameNone — already split
player_last_namePlayerLastNameNone — already split
genderGenderNone — already M/F
birth_dateDOBNone — already MM/DD/YYYY
parent1_emailFatherEmailAddressNone (Father = Parent1, not gendered)
parent1_first_nameFatherFirstNameNone — already split
parent1_last_nameFatherLastNameNone — already split
parent1_mobile_numberFatherCellPhone(XXX) XXX-XXXX → XXX-XXX-XXXX
parent2_emailMotherEmailAddressNone (Mother = Parent2)
parent2_first_nameMotherFirstNameNone — already split
parent2_last_nameMotherLastNameNone — already split
parent2_mobile_numberMotherCellPhone(XXX) XXX-XXXX → XXX-XXX-XXXX
streetAddress1None
cityCityNone
stateStateNone
zipZIPCode91607-3715 → 91607 (truncate +4)
team—Always blank — SA has prior season teams that don't exist in PM. Teams built fresh after registration.
💡 "Father" and "Mother" = Parent1 and Parent2 The SA column names say "Father" and "Mother" but they're not gendered — they're simply Parent1 and Parent2. Many "Father" entries have female names and vice versa. The tool maps them as-is to parent1 and parent2 in the PM import.
5
Review the Output CSVs

Open the CSV files in Excel or a text editor and spot-check before submitting.

6
Send BC-Verified File to PlayMetrics

PlayMetrics must import the BC-verified file on their end — you cannot do this yourself. They flag these players as BC-verified in the system so returning families skip the BC upload during registration.

  1. Email success@playmetrics.com
  2. Subject: "BC-Verified Player Import — [Your Region Name]"
  3. Attach the playmetrics_bc_verified_YYYYMMDD.csv file
  4. Mention that it's the standard Player Import CSV format with BC-verified players only
  5. Wait for confirmation that the import is complete before proceeding
✅ How BC Skip Works After Import Once PM imports these players as BC-verified, any player who registers and matches an imported record will automatically skip the BC upload question. New players (not in the import) will be prompted to upload their BC. The system handles both cases — no conditional question needed.
7
Import Non-Verified Players Yourself (Optional)

If the tool produced a non-verified CSV (players without a BC on file), you can import these yourself in PlayMetrics admin. If all your players had BC on file, the tool won't produce this file — skip this step.

  1. Log in to PlayMetrics admin
  2. Navigate to Players
  3. Click More Actions → Import Players
  4. Upload the playmetrics_non_verified_YYYYMMDD.csv file
  5. Map columns if prompted (they should auto-match since we used the standard template)
  6. Confirm the import
8
Verify Imported Data

After both imports are complete, spot-check records in PlayMetrics.

Requirements

PlatformWhat You Need
WindowsPlayMetricsImport.exe — no Python needed. Download from GitHub Releases.
Mac / Linuxplaymetrics_import.py + Python 3 with pip3 install pandas openpyxl. Download the script from the GitHub repo.

Batch Mode (Recommended)

Windows: PlayMetricsImport.exe --dir C:\Users\you\sa_reports
Mac / Linux: python3 playmetrics_import.py --dir ~/sa_reports

Auto-detects all playerUpload*.xlsx and Player*Photo*BC*.xlsx files in the folder. Handles underscores, spaces, and year suffixes like _2025. Merges multiple seasons automatically.

Interactive Mode

Windows: PlayMetricsImport.exe
Mac / Linux: python3 playmetrics_import.py

Prompts for each file. Output goes to playmetrics_output/ folder.
